title: Good Friday
hook: no Mass anywhere; people come forward to venerate the cross
carry: the one day with no mass

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Triduum: three days kept as one feast, beginning with a towel and a basin. Your line was the three holiest days begin. Today, the second of the three.

Three o'clock on a Friday afternoon. The church is bare: no cloth on the altar, no candles, no flowers. The tabernacle is empty, its door hanging open. No opening hymn. The priest and the deacon walk in without a word, and then, in front of everyone, they lie face down on the floor, or kneel, and stay there. The whole church is silent with them. It's the strangest entrance of the year, on the one afternoon when no Mass is said anywhere in the Catholic world.
screen: `THREE O'CLOCK.` → `A BARE CHURCH.` → `FACE DOWN ON THE FLOOR.`

segments.voice: Three o'clock because the Gospels say Jesus died at about the ninth hour, mid-afternoon. No Mass because, by a very old tradition, the Church doesn't celebrate it on this day at all. Holy Saturday stays quiet too, until the vigil after dark. Instead comes the Celebration of the Lord's Passion, in three parts. First, the word. The whole Passion is read from John's Gospel, often with the congregation speaking the crowd's lines, so everyone has to say crucify him out loud. In John, Jesus's last words are, "It is consummated." Finished, completed, brought to its end. Second, the prayers: ten long intercessions, for the Church, for the Pope and the clergy, for the Jewish people, for those who don't believe in God, for leaders, for the suffering. On the day it remembers his death, the Church prays for the whole world by name. Third, the cross. A wooden cross is carried in or unveiled, and the priest sings three times, in Latin or the local language, behold the wood of the cross. People come forward one by one to venerate it: a bow, a genuflection, a hand on the wood, a kiss. Then Communion is given from hosts consecrated the night before, and everyone leaves in silence. Catholics also fast today. And the name? Nobody is completely sure why English says good. Most likely it meant holy, an older sense of the word. In German it's the Friday of mourning.
screen: `NO MASS, BY ANCIENT TRADITION.` · `THE PASSION: IT IS CONSUMMATED.` · `PRAYERS FOR THE WHOLE WORLD.` · `BEHOLD THE WOOD OF THE CROSS.`

segments.voice: Keep a small piece of the quiet hour at three o'clock: turn off whatever is making noise, and picture a plain wooden cross with a long line of people walking up to it, one at a time. If you pray, bring someone who is suffering with you to the cross; if you don't, simply keep the silence, as the whole church does today.
Good Friday. The day Christians remember the death of Jesus, with no Mass, a long silence, and a line of people at the cross. Today's word.
Your line: the one day with no mass. Only the word, the prayers and the cross. That's day one hundred fifty-two.

howItsDone: On Good Friday Catholics attend the Celebration of the Lord's Passion, usually in the afternoon: the Passion from John is read, the Church prays the solemn intercessions, and people come forward to venerate the cross; adults also fast and abstain from meat.

chat.says: Is there a special Mass on Good Friday?
options: No. It's the one day with no Mass: the Passion, the prayers and the cross.
Yes, the longest Mass of the year, held at three in the afternoon.
Yes, but only the priest attends; everyone else prays at home.
chat.meaning: By a very old tradition, no Mass is said on Good Friday; the Celebration of the Lord's Passion has the word, prayers and the cross.

Passion.meaning: the story of Jesus's suffering and death, read from John

intercessions.meaning: long prayers for the Church and the whole world

notes: Carry says 'the one day with no mass'. Strictly, no Mass is celebrated on Good Friday or during Holy Saturday until the Easter Vigil after nightfall; the script says so plainly. A Keeper may want to adjust the index carry.
Rubrics: priest and deacon prostrate or kneel in silence at the start; the celebration takes place about three in the afternoon unless pastoral reasons suggest later. Confirm.

Ten solemn intercessions in the current Missal (Church, Pope, clergy and faithful, catechumens, unity of Christians, Jewish people, those who do not believe in Christ, those who do not believe in God, those in public office, those in tribulation). The script names a selection. Confirm.
Ecce lignum Crucis, in quo salus mundi pependit. Venite, adoremus: sung three times. Ecclesiastical pronunciation given approximately.
Origin of 'Good' uncertain; 'God's Friday' theory is widely doubted. German Karfreitag from Old High German kara (lament). Check.
Fasting and abstinence on Good Friday: canon 1251. Paraphrased.
